edition.window: Orders and decisions passed or reported between 10:00 AM IST on 26 November 2026 and 10:00 AM IST on 27 November 2026

items.caseName: Pashupati Corporation v. Rakesh Dugar & Uttam Tekriwal
items.coram: Justice Sharad Kumar Sharma (Judicial Member), Arun Baroka (Technical Member)
items.headline: RP cannot use one company's CIRP to attack a sale made in another company's liquidation
items.text: The NCLAT held that a resolution professional cannot treat one corporate debtor's insolvency process as a forum to collaterally challenge a sale in a separate liquidation. It also faulted the NCLT for not impleading the auction purchaser, who was a necessary party. The order was set aside and the matter remanded for fresh decision within about three months.

items.caseName: Microtek International Pvt. Ltd. v. Anil Gupta & Ors.
items.coram: Yogesh Khanna (Judicial Member), Barun Mitra and Ajia Das Mehrotra (Technical Members)
items.headline: E&Y benchmarking report to go on record in Microtek oppression case
items.text: The NCLAT directed the NCLT Delhi to take the E&Y benchmarking report on record, finding no prejudice since both sides relied on it and the respondents had themselves sought it. It noted that neither the Companies Act, 2013 nor the NCLT Rules, 2016 bars filing documents after pleadings close, before a final order.

items.caseName: Jineshwar Siddagouda Patil v. Jamakhandi Sugars Ltd. & Ors.
items.coram: Sunil Kumar Aggarwal (Judicial Member), Radhakrishna Sreepada (Technical Member)
items.headline: Jamakhandi Sugars EGM may go ahead, but resolutions held back pending share-payment check
items.text: Relying on LIC v. Escorts, the NCLT allowed the requisitioned EGM to proceed but barred implementation of resolutions until the company verifies whether 49 shareholders actually paid for their shares. It restrained transfer or encumbrance of company assets and froze the board's composition; the matter is listed on 7 December 2026.

items.caseName: Neyveli Lignite Corporation v. Commissioner of GST & Central Excise
items.coram: P. Dinesha (Judicial Member), M. Ajit Kumar (Technical Member)
items.headline: Free housing and facilities for CISF personnel not part of taxable security service value
items.text: CESTAT Chennai held that accommodation, utilities and medical facilities given to CISF personnel are not automatically consideration for security services, even though the contract required them. The department failed to show they were agreed extra payment, and service tax had already been paid on deployment charges, so the demand, interest and penalties were set aside.

items.caseName: Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams v. Commissioner of Central Tax, Tirupati - CGST
items.coram: Angad Prasad (Judicial Member), Sanjiv Srivastava (Technical Member)
items.headline: Rs 2.25 crore service tax demand on TTD pilgrim accommodation set aside and remanded
items.text: The tribunal held that exemption under Sl. No. 5(a) of Notification 25/2012-ST must be tested facility by facility, rejecting both a blanket exemption on religious status and a blanket denial. It remanded the matter to examine low-tariff units, cum-tax benefit, penalties and reasonable cause after a personal hearing.

items.headline: CENVAT credit allowed on service tax paid on natural gas short off-take compensation
items.text: CESTAT Chandigarh allowed Maruti Suzuki's appeal, holding that service tax paid on compensation to GAIL for short off-take of natural gas qualifies for CENVAT credit. The roughly Rs 8.56 crore payment under a minimum-offtake agreement was held directly related to procurement of inputs.

items.caseName: Vera Display and Storage Products Private Limited v. The Commissioner of Keralam State GST, Thiruvananthapuram
items.coram: Subramanya Rayaprol (Vice President), Ramamoorthi Sriram (Technical Member)
items.headline: Missing e-way bill for IGST-paid imported goods only a procedural lapse
items.text: GSTAT Ernakulam held that not generating an e-way bill for imported goods on which IGST was already paid is a procedural lapse absent evasion or concealment. The e-way bill was generated after interception while goods were detained; the appeal was allowed and the bank guarantee ordered released within two weeks.

items.caseName: Rajnish Jha & Anr. v. Maharashtra Real Estate Regulatory Authority & Ors.
items.coram: S. S. Shinde (Chairperson), Shrikant M. Deshpande (Accountant Member)
items.headline: No two-thirds homebuyer consent needed when promoter firm converts to company with same owners
items.text: The Maharashtra REAT held that Section 15 RERA consent of two-thirds allottees is not required where a partnership firm converts into a private company with unchanged shareholding, though RERA approval is still needed. All co-promoters remain jointly and severally liable; the promoters were barred from creating third-party rights and told to honour the 2018 agreement for sale.

items.headline: Sale proceeds of flat transferred by company to director not 'other income'
items.text: ITAT Delhi deleted a Rs 2.20 crore addition, holding that sale proceeds of a flat given by a company to its director were not taxable as income from other sources. The tribunal relied on the assessee's proven ownership and possession of the flat since 2005.

items.headline: Stamp duty value on agreement date applies where advance paid by cheque: Section 56(2)(x)
items.text: ITAT Lucknow directed the AO to adopt the stamp duty value on the date of agreement, not registration, since part consideration was paid by account-payee cheque before the agreement. The AO had added Rs 66.46 lakh using the registration-date value and must now recompute.

items.headline: Agricultural land capital gains remanded to verify distance from municipal limits
items.text: For AY 2011-12, ITAT Delhi sent the capital gains issue on sale of agricultural land back to the CIT(A). Municipal and RTI records conflicted on the land's distance from municipal limits, which decides taxability under the 8 km test, so fresh verification was ordered.

items.caseName: The Institution Management Committee of ITI
items.headline: Wrong ITR form no ground to deny Section 10(23C)(iiiad) exemption to society
items.text: ITAT Nagpur held that a registered society cannot lose its Section 10(23C)(iiiad) exemption merely for filing in the wrong ITR form. For AY 2017-18 the society had filed ITR-5 and then a revised return; the AO was directed to allow the Rs 22.58 lakh claim.
